elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each Party)
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed"

elements.element: Cap amount is the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"
"neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect or consequential damages"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims ... a Party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations ... are not \"damages\" for purposes of this Section 10.9"

elements.element: Fallback: mutual cap of 12 months' fees
elements.evidence: cap is "the greater of" 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, not a flat 12 months' fees cap

elements.element: Fallback: carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud"

reasons: All twelve atomic elements of the preferred position are present in the inserted Section 10.9: mutual aggregate cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, the full uncapped carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP infringement), and the payment-obligations carve-out from "damages".
The document contained no liability cap at all, so a concise inserted clause is the minimal route; nothing in the untouched headings/counterparts provision or elsewhere was altered.

The clause uses the alias "Customer" although the defined party is "Company"; the immediate gloss "meaning all amounts due from the Company under this Agreement" ties it to the defined party, so no dangling or undefined mechanic results. Worth a drafting tidy to say "Company's payment obligations" but not a substantive defect.

Fallback is not independently satisfied because it requires a flat 12 months' fees cap; that is immaterial here since the locked preferred level is fully met and the greater-of formulation is more favourable to us.
